title: Azolla filiculoides Sporocarp Cryo-Preservation
author: Paul Brouwer
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.9bdh2i6

steps.title: Collect and batch megasporocarps
steps.instruction: Gather mature megasporocarps with sporocarps attached from culture sediment. Form experimental batches of 20–50 megasporocarps for cryoprotectant tests (evaluated in duplicate) or larger batches of 247–391 megasporocarps for drying tests.

steps.title: Apply cryoprotectant pre‑treatment
steps.instruction: Add exactly 1 mL of the chosen cryoprotective solution to each batch immediately before snap‑freezing.

steps.title: Apply drying pre‑treatment
steps.instruction: Dry megasporocarps in a fume hood at room temperature for 1, 4, or 8 days, **or** place them in an oven at a constant 26 °C for 7 days. No fluid is added before snap‑freezing.

steps.title: Snap‑freeze in liquid nitrogen
steps.instruction: Immerse each batch (whether cryoprotectant‑treated or dried) in liquid nitrogen for exactly 5 minutes.

steps.title: Transfer to –80 °C freezer
steps.instruction: After snap‑freezing, move the tubes to a –80 °C freezer for indefinite storage (viability confirmed up to 4 years).

steps.title: Thaw and wash recovered samples
steps.instruction: Place frozen tubes on a heating plate set to 30 °C for 1.5 minutes. For cryoprotectant‑treated batches, wash the megasporocarps three times with 1 mL of Azolla growth medium. For dried batches, add 1 mL of medium after thawing. Then transfer the megasporocarps (with massulae attached) into 400 µL of Azolla growth medium at pH 5.5 and incubate in a growth cabinet set to 25 °C day / 15 °C night, 12 h light at 40–70 µmol s⁻¹ m⁻² PPFD.

steps.title: Include appropriate controls
steps.instruction: For each cryopreservation protocol, run a treatment control that receives the pre‑treatment but is not frozen, and run two additional controls that receive neither pre‑treatment nor freezing.

steps.title: Optional wet storage
steps.instruction: Megasporocarps and microsporocarps may be stored wet in water at 4 °C for up to 4 years.
